articles.title: Arc Mainnet launching Sept. 16 with major founding validators
articles.summary: Circle's Q2 update confirmed Arc Mainnet launches September 16 with founding validators including BlackRock, DTCC, Galaxy, Mastercard, MoneyGram, Standard Chartered, and Visa. The company also received a federal trust bank charter from the OCC for Circle National Trust, and said USDC captured nearly 70% of stablecoin transaction volume in June per Visa Onchain Analytics. CEO Jeremy Allaire separately noted these institutions join over 100 ecosystem and institutional builders already on Arc's private mainnet.

articles.title: Bitcoin activity hits 2026 high amid Coldcard attack as K33 flags potential bottoming pattern
articles.summary: K33 says roughly 890,000 BTC moved onchain over the past week, the highest seven-day active supply of 2026, coinciding with the expanding Coldcard exploit, which Galaxy Research now estimates involves at least 15 attackers and roughly $130 million (~2,000 BTC) in losses. K33's Vetle Lunde said such spikes in active supply have historically coincided with local market tops and bottoms, arguing "panic is visible onchain" as holders react to hardware wallet security concerns and price declines.

articles.title: Blockspace: Connecting the World to Ethereum
articles.summary: Blockspace, an Ethereum infrastructure company founded by the Gattaca and ultra sound teams, launched with a BlueYard-led funding round that also included ether.fi Ventures, Quasar Builder, Sharplink, Breed VC, Luganodes, and Stakely, targeting gaps in the out-of-protocol infrastructure that carries more than 90% of Ethereum's blockspace. The company monetizes in ETH by operating staking infrastructure, capturing transaction fees from blocks its staked ETH proposes, and compounding those earnings back into stake. To limit centralization risk, Blockspace self-caps its ETH holdings at 15% of total stake, a threshold the Ethereum community has cited as responsible. The launch positions Blockspace as the commercial arm of the open-source Blockspace Forum and is timed ahead of anticipated ePBS implementation, which the team expects to reshape block production economics.

articles.title: The Permaweb as a Substrate for AI
articles.summary: AO, a hyper-parallel compute layer built on Arweave, provides AI agents a trustless substrate by eliminating dependencies on centralized API keys, model providers, and human-provisioned infrastructure, letting agents self-provision via a generated keypair that serves as identity, account, and payment method simultaneously. Every AO computation produces a signed hashpath, a chain of receipts any party can replay, making inference verifiability a structural byproduct of execution rather than a separate audit layer. The HyperBEAM Agent Device Stack composes inference, TEE GPU attestation, stateless tool loops, and containerized execution as modular devices over plain HTTP, with full agent state persisting on Arweave's permanent message log at a one-time cost of ~$22/GiB. Apus Network demonstrates this with a keyless OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving gemma-3-27b-it on H100 in confidential-computing mode, returning TEE attestation quotes published to Arweave for post-hoc verification.

articles.title: 7 Projects Building the Payment Rails for the Agent Economy
articles.summary: Traditional payment rails cannot serve AI agents because card networks' OTP, 3D Secure, and chargeback requirements assume a human operator, and Stripe's $0.30 flat fee consumed 97% of the ~$0.31 median agent spend in 2025. Incumbents are responding through acquisitions (Stripe took Privy and Bridge, Mastercard acquired BVNK) and pilots (Visa's stablecoin settlement reached a $7B run rate), while seven crypto-native projects are building dedicated infrastructure across the stack. The cohort spans a purpose-built EVM L1 (Kite AI, $35M from PayPal, Coinbase Ventures, and General Catalyst, with Google A2P and PYUSD as launch partners), x402-native facilitators (PayAI's 35.8M transactions processed. Thirdweb's pay-per-call API layer), stablecoin orchestration to resolve gas/payment token mismatches (Eco), full-stack agent wallets with virtual card issuance via Visa and Mastercard partnerships (Crossmint), and a co-wallet protocol embedding budget mandates in x402/A2A/MCP calls with ZK-batched settlement (FluxA's AEP2). PaymanAI, backed by $13.8M from Visa, Circle, and Coinbase, closes the set by targeting banks and credit unions with agent-driven transaction execution, audit trails, and kill switches.

articles.title: The Simple Economics of L1 Value Capture
articles.summary: Written ahead of Solana governance votes on SIMD 550 (Double Disinflation Speed) and SIMD 553 (Resource Fees), this piece applies equity valuation theory to L1 token economics, arguing that inflation-funded staking rewards dilute non-stakers without producing protocol revenue, while fee burns and distributions to stakers are the sole mechanisms that generate tokenholder surplus. Gas demand elasticity estimates derived from EIP-1559 pricing data put short-term price sensitivity at 0.6 to 0.8, meaning a 10% fee increase reduces transaction volume by 6 to 8%, and uniform fee schedules fail to capture the willingness-to-pay spread across heterogeneous users. The author proposes value-based fee instruments, charging a percentage of transfer notional rather than flat compute costs, as a more precise revenue approach than compute pricing alone. Solana and Ethereum's accumulated network effects in liquidity, applications, and infrastructure give their fee streams more pricing power than current market valuations reflect.

articles.title: Proof of Play Ceases Operations, Open-Sources Pirate Nation
articles.summary: Proof of Play, the blockchain gaming studio behind the fully onchain Pirate Nation, is ceasing operations after failing to build a sustainable product proving blockchain gaming's thesis at scale. The team is open-sourcing the Pirate Nation Unity app, smart contracts, and an internal agent workflow tool, while releasing Founder Pirates NFTs and all Pirate Nation artwork and IP under CC0. Proof of Play points carry no redemption value, though the independent Pirate Nation Foundation will continue supporting the $PIRATE token, and Shiba Story Go! has been acquired by a third party and will continue operating.

articles.title: Fintech infrastructure is commoditized; the moat is brand & distribution
articles.summary: A small team can assemble a fully functional neobank for under $60,000 by stitching together APIs from providers like Dakota, Blend, MoonPay, Privy/Turnkey, Portola, and Rain, meaning the competitive edge has shifted from unique technology to user experience, distribution strength, customer support, and trusted branding.

articles.title: Rejected Western Union card application taught them
articles.summary: The Rain-powered Western Union card only funds via Western Union's own Solana-based stablecoin USDPT, targets high-inflation markets like Argentina, lets recipients receive transfers directly as USDPT, and connects digitally to Western Union's 360,000+ cash pickup locations.

articles.title: RedotPay leads crypto card downloads despite 0% cashback
articles.summary: RedotPay recorded about 300K installs last month versus Bitget Wallet's 110K, reporting over 7 million users across 100+ countries and $5 billion in cumulative spend, driven by P2P trading, bank/e-wallet payouts in 21 currencies, and a Telegram Mini App rather than cashback incentives.

articles.title: New storage credits cut gas costs for repeat clear-and-create workflows
articles.summary: Tempo's new storage credit system offsets ~98% of storage creation costs when a contract clears eligible storage and later creates more within the same transaction, benefiting repeat-workflow apps like DEX order placement and cancellation.

articles.title: x402 agentic payment standard gains momentum
articles.summary: Cloudflare's new agentic wallet/identity system and last month's Monetization Gateway add to growing infrastructure support.
